(a) In General.—Subparagraph (G) of section 170(e)(6) is amended by striking “December 31, 2009” and inserting “December 31, 2011”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to contributions made in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2009.

fable.w: This section only extends a sunset date in a tax deduction provision (section 170(e)(6)) and sets an effective date for contributions. There is no tempting participation reading: it has no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

opus.w: This section only moves a tax deduction's expiration date from December 31, 2009 to December 31, 2011 and sets the amendment's effective date. It requires no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. "Contributions" here means charitable donations under the tax code, not outside parties taking part in a federal decision.
opus.s: Subparagraph (G) of section 170(e)(6) is amended by striking “December 31, 2009” and inserting “December 31, 2011”.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply amends a date in the Internal Revenue Code and specifies the effective date of that amendment. It does not require or recommend any consultation, public comment, hearing, or coordination with outside parties. The text is purely legislative directive regarding statutory dates.
qwen_chat.s:
(a) In General.—Subparagraph (G) of section 170(e)(6) is amended by striking “December 31, 2009” and inserting “December 31, 2011”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to contributions made in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2009.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending tax code provisions affects the public, but the text itself contains no mechanism for public input, consultation, or participation. It is a straightforward legislative amendment to dates and effective periods.
